## Parent

#121 — spec: Expected-set entry resolves its skill files

## What to build

Deployment stops reading a directory-level resolution status and judges each entry by the skill files it owns. A partial checkout stays usable for development, and a release refuses to ship when any expected skill file is missing — including the case where a skill directory exists but its root `SKILL.md` was deleted.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The development provisioning flow warns about and skips an entry with a missing skill file, and keeps provisioning every resolved entry exactly as before (partial checkout remains usable).
- [ ] Packaging fails when any expected skill file is missing, and the error names every missing file — including the "directory exists, root `SKILL.md` missing" state.
- [ ] Packaging still refuses to ship on a missing source directory and on a malformed lock file, naming the offending lock file.
- [ ] Tarball layout, `manifest.json` content, and installed file layout are unchanged; contents and manifest still derive from one enumeration.
- [ ] Existing development and packaging tests stay green, with new coverage for the missing-root-`SKILL.md` case; any fixture that mirrors the old entry-level resolution status migrates without changing the asserted outcome.

## Blocked by

- #122 — Expected-set entry resolves its skill files (expand).
title: Dev and pack consume skill files; release gate names every missing file
